title: Cuentos de la selva
author: Horacio Quiroga
blurb: Eight animal stories from the forest of Misiones, written for children: a turtle, flamingos, a parrot and a war of alligators.
note: Published in 1918, so it is in the US public domain (published before 1931).
coverCredit: Henri Rousseau, Surprised! (Tiger in a Tropical Storm), 1891. National Gallery, London. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

title: Platero y yo
author: Juan Ramón Jiménez
blurb: Short, gentle chapters about a poet and his small donkey in an Andalusian village.
note: The first edition came out in 1914, so it is in the US public domain (published before 1931). The old spelling of the preposition a (written á) is modernized.
coverCredit: Modesto Teixidor, Women Riding a Donkey, about 1890. Museo Art Nouveau y Art Déco Casa Lis, Salamanca. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

title: La Edad de Oro (selección)
author: José Martí
blurb: Stories and poems José Martí wrote for the children of the Americas: three liberators, a rich boy and his poor cousin, a girl's old black doll, a magic shrimp and a pair of pink shoes.
note: Published in 1889 as a monthly for children by an author who died in 1895, so it is in the public domain worldwide.
coverCredit: Joaquín Sorolla, Strolling along the Seashore (Paseo a orillas del mar), 1909. Museo Sorolla, Madrid. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

title: Ratón Pérez
author: Luis Coloma
blurb: Little King Buby loses his first tooth, and Ratón Pérez, the mouse who comes for children's teeth, takes him across Madrid to the home of a poor boy.
note: Written in the early 1890s for the boy king Alfonso XIII and printed in this edition in 1911; the author died in 1915, so it is in the public domain worldwide. The old spellings á, ó and é of the words a, o and e are modernized.
coverCredit: Francisco Domingo Marqués, Alfonso XIII as a Child, 1889. Patrimonio Nacional, Royal Collections, Madrid. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

title: Cuentos de amor, de locura y de muerte (selección)
author: Horacio Quiroga
blurb: Four dark stories: a snakebite in the jungle, a feather pillow, a hen, and a sunstroke.
note: Published in 1917, so it is in the US public domain (published before 1931).
coverCredit: Henri Rousseau, The Snake Charmer, 1907. Musée d’Orsay, Paris. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

title: Leyendas (selección)
author: Gustavo Adolfo Bécquer
blurb: Three legends of Spain: green eyes in a spring, the haunted hill of souls, and a ray of moonlight.
note: Written in the 1860s, the author died in 1870. The old spelling of the preposition a (written á) is modernized.
coverCredit: Valeriano Bécquer, Portrait of Gustavo Adolfo Bécquer, his brother, 1862. Museo de Bellas Artes de Sevilla. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

title: El sombrero de tres picos
author: Pedro Antonio de Alarcón
blurb: A miller, his clever wife, and a lecherous magistrate in a comic night of mistaken identities.
note: Published in 1874 and the author died in 1891, so it is in the US public domain.
coverCredit: Francisco de Goya, The Parasol (El quitasol), 1777. Museo del Prado, Madrid. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

title: ¡Adiós, Cordera! y otros cuentos
author: Leopoldo Alas «Clarín»
blurb: Five stories by Clarín, led by his most famous: two children in Asturias, their old cow Cordera, and the railway that takes her away.
note: Collected in El Señor y lo demás, son cuentos in 1893 (this text follows the 1919 printing), and the author died in 1901, so it is in the public domain worldwide.
coverCredit: Rosa Bonheur, A Shepherdess with a Goat and Two Cows in a Meadow, about 1842–45. Dahesh Museum of Art, New York. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

title: La vida de Lazarillo de Tormes
author: Anónimo
blurb: A poor boy serves a string of masters, from a blind beggar to a priest, and learns to live by his wits.
note: Published in 1554 by an unknown author, so it is in the public domain worldwide.
coverCredit: Bartolomé Esteban Murillo, The Young Beggar, about 1645–50. Musée du Louvre, Paris. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

title: Marianela
author: Benito Pérez Galdós
blurb: A girl who has always led a blind young man around a mining village fears what will happen when he can see.
note: Published in 1878 and the author died in 1920, so it is in the US public domain.
coverCredit: Francisco de Goya, The Blind Guitarist (El ciego de la guitarra), 1778. Museo del Prado, Madrid. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

title: Don Quijote de la Mancha (primera parte)
author: Miguel de Cervantes
blurb: A country gentleman reads so many tales of chivalry that he sets out as a knight errant, with Sancho Panza as his squire, and mistakes windmills for giants.
note: Published in 1605 by an author who died in 1616, so it is in the public domain worldwide. This is the whole first part, chapters I to LII, without the prologue and prefatory verses.
coverCredit: Gustave Doré, Don Quixote among his books, engraved by Héliodore Pisan for Don Quixote, 1863. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

title: El gaucho Martín Fierro
author: José Hernández
blurb: A gaucho sings his own life in verse: sent to the frontier, robbed of his home and family, he becomes an outlaw on the pampa. The national poem of Argentina.
note: Published in 1872 by an author who died in 1886, so it is in the public domain worldwide. A few slips of the transcription are corrected from the 1894 printing.
coverCredit: Juan Manuel Blanes, One of the Three Chiripás (Uno de los tres chiripás), about 1881. Museo Nacional de Artes Visuales, Montevideo. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.
